title: From Human Corrections to Learned Segmentations: A Critical Mathematical Review of Information, Learning, and Human Effort
abstract: arXiv:2610.20396v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When does a human correction become useful learning, and what establishes better segmentation at matched human effort? This critical narrative review follows feedback through its selection, learner update, and evaluation. It compares active learning, machine teaching, interactive segmentation, and sequential predictive evaluation using a common mathematical account of target information, predictive error, response predictability, and human work. An exact Bayesian update converts evaluation-label information into expected log-loss improvement; an excess-risk decomposition explains what an approximate learner can lose. Conditional information decompositions separate the roles of selected locations, labels, and displayed context. Empirical comparisons show why response protocols, update mechanisms, and effort denominators matter, distinguishing current-mask refinement from reusable learning and simulated interaction from human evidence. translated_title: 从人类纠错到可学习的分割：关于信息、学习与人类付出的批判性数学综述
translated_abstract: 人类的纠错何时才能成为有用的学习？在同等人类付出的条件下，又是什么决定了更好的分割效果？这篇批判性叙述性综述追踪反馈从选择、学习器更新到评估的完整过程。它基于一个统一的数学框架——涵盖目标信息、预测误差、响应可预测性与人类工作量——对主动学习、机器教学、交互式分割和顺序预测评估进行比较。精确的贝叶斯更新将评估标签信息转化为预期的对数损失改进；超额风险分解则解释了近似学习器可能损失什么。条件信息分解将所选位置、标签以及所展示上下文的作用区分开来。实证比较说明了响应协议、更新机制和付出衡量标准为何至关重要，并区分了针对当前掩码的优化与可复用的学习，以及模拟交互与真实人类证据之间的差别。
tldr: 该综述提出统一的数学框架，借助精确贝叶斯更新、超额风险分解与条件信息分解，系统比较主动学习、机器教学和交互式分割等方法，阐明人类纠错何时转化为有效学习，以及在同等人类付出下如何衡量与实现更好的分割效果。
en_tdlr: This critical mathematical review establishes a unified framework—using exact Bayesian updates, excess-risk decomposition, and conditional information decompositions—to compare active learning, machine teaching, and interactive segmentation, clarifying when human corrections become useful learning and what yields better segmentation at matched human effort.
